item.title: Step Into the World of Vector Control: Free Family-Friendly Open House — Sat Sep 19, 11:00 AM — Marin/Sonoma Mosquito and Vector Control District
item.description: Step behind the scenes and discover how the Marin/Sonoma Mosquito and Vector Control District works year-round to protect public health. This free, family-friendly event invites residents of all ages to explore hands-on activities, interactive displays, and live demonstrations that highlight the District’s Integrated Vector Management Program. Educational displays will showcase mosquito and tick surveillance methods used to identify and prevent emerging threats to public health, non-toxic rodent control strategies, and simple tips for reducing mosquito sources around the home. Guests can learn how mosquito traps work, meet the vector control technicians who respond to service requests, and leave with practical, easy-to-use information to help protect their families and neighborhoods. item.title: Saturday Live Music at Spicy Vines feat. S.R. Laws — Sat Sep 19, 3:00 PM — Spicy Vines
item.description:
Where unforgettable wines, live music, and good vibes come together. Join us every Saturday from 3–6 PM at Spicy Vines for a tasting room experience like no other — where top local musicians from across the Bay Area meet our award-winning small-lot wines. From Rock & Roll and Blues to Jazz, Bluegrass, and Americana, each weekend brings new sounds and new reasons to raise a glass. S.R. Laws Rooted in Northern California and shaped by a lifetime of musical discovery, singer-songwriter, S.R. Laws, crafts heartfelt songs with slow-burning passion and vivid storytelling. Now based in Sonoma County, he tours and performs original rock with his band, The Heartsleeves, drawing listeners in with melodies inspired by legends like John Hiatt, Rodney Crowell, and Neil Finn. item.title: Public Star Party — Sat Sep 19, 8:00 PM — Robert Ferguson Observatory
item.description: Public Star Parties are the heart of the Robert Ferguson Observatory—your monthly invitation to experience the wonder of the night sky like never before. Whether you’re a lifelong astronomy enthusiast or simply curious about what lies beyond our planet, these gatherings offer something magical for everyone. Each month includes a variety of engaging astronomy presentations led by our expert docents. You’ll hear fascinating stories about the cosmos and the science behind some of the objects you’ll soon be observing. These talks set the stage for an unforgettable night under the stars. Step outside into the darkness of Sugarloaf Ridge State Park, where the skies open up in breathtaking clarity. You’ll have the chance to explore the universe through three of RFO’s massive telescopes, each powerful enough to reveal extraordinary detail: lunar craters, planets, star clusters, glowing nebulae, distant galaxies, and more. item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Sep 20, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Let's Play Chinese Mahjong! — Sun Sep 20, 2:00 PM — Cloverdale Library
item.description:
Learn to play Chinese \(Hong Kong-style\) mahjong, or come play with friends if you already know the game! We will have sets and instructors on site to teach the game and help with rules and scoring. Mahjong is a game for multi-generations; it keeps the mind sharp with a basic set of rules that can be learned in 30 minutes, and adds unending ways to add strategy and challenge; it builds community and sustains culture; it's fun and addicting in a wholesome way! 'Four Flowers Mahjong Salon' goal is to bring mahjong to the Sonoma County area. They currently teach at private homes, farmers markets, tasting rooms, and coffee shops!
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: GPGS: New Roots at Scribe — Tue Sep 22, 5:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Museum of Art
item.description: Hosted by Scribe and SVMA Join us for a special golden-hour evening at The Hacienda at Scribe Winery, one of Sonoma’s most distinctive Wine Country destinations. Enjoy Scribe wines and seasonal bites as we gather among the historic Hacienda, lush gardens, and sweeping vineyard views—a beautiful setting where wine, design, history, and California style come together. Founded by fourth-generation California farmers Andrew and Adam Mariani, Scribe occupies a storied property with roots reaching back to Sonoma’s earliest winemaking days. At the heart of the estate is its remarkable 19th-century Hacienda, lovingly revived by Bill Schaeffer, Project Director at Cello & Maudru Construction, with architect David Darling of Aidlin Darling Design. During the evening, Bill will share brief remarks about the restoration, offering a glimpse into both the challenges and the charm of bringing this historic place back to life. item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Sep 24, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Sep 25, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
